transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 min
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Cho (Redwood CSM); Aisha Kwan (Hypernova Procurement), Luca Romano (Legal), Priya Singh (CTO), Diego Flores (Cloud Ops)

Summary: quick procurement/contract handoff after pilot. focus on MSA redlines, DPA specifics (data residency, subprocessors, KMS), SLA thresholds and egress fees. pricing path (hosted vs dedicated) and technical acceptance benchmarks.

Topics: MSA exceptions, DPA encryption/KMS, SLA credit model, dedicated capacity pricing, egress & network fees, pilot acceptance criteria, escrow/termination rights.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we, um, appreciate you squeezing this in right after your exec review. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha: Yeah, hi this is Aisha Kwan, head of procurement at Hypernova.
[00:09] Luca: Luca here, legal counsel, thanks.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, CTO.
[00:12] Diego: Diego, cloud ops.
[00:14] Jordan: Great. Sofia, you want to intro?
[00:16] Sofia: Sure, hi all, Sofia Patel, solutions engineer, I looked at the pilot results and some of the latency spikes, we'll talk about capacity options.
[00:25] Evan: Evan Cho, customer success, I'll be helping with onboarding and the billing piece.
[00:29] Jordan: Cool. Okay agenda: MSA redlines and DPA, SLA and egress, pricing tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated), and next steps. Luca, before we jump in any must-have clauses from legal?
[00:39] Luca: Yes couple of items. We want explicit data residency control, must be able to restrict processing to EU regions for EU customers, also we want KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and, um, a stronger audit log SLA. Also review of subprocessors list and a right-to-audit clause.
[00:54] Jordan: Great, that aligns with our Private offering but we can also do dedicated in-region for Hosted customers. Sofia, maybe run through options.
[01:02] Sofia: Yeah, so high level there are three paths: 1) Hosted API with EU region pinning — fastest but limited key control, 2) Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools in customer's region with customer-managed KMS option and better network egress predictability, 3) Private (VPC/on-prem) which is the full compliance option. For Hypernova's volumes you probably want Dedicated but we should look at cost.
[01:28] Priya: Diego, do we have a hard requirement for KMS? We prefer CMK for encryption at rest.
[01:33] Diego: yes, CMK required, and we need SSO/SAML integration with our IdP for admin access. Also we want minimal cross-border transfer.
[01:40] Jordan: Noted. Luca, on audit rights and right-to-audit—we usually provide SOC2 report and can support contractual right-to-audit with reasonable notice windows. Full on-site audits are heavier, we can discuss escrow for source or configuration if needed.
[01:52] Luca: SOC2 is fine as baseline, but we're seeing buyers ask for either contractual audit rights or escrow for critical configs. Any precedent?
[01:59] Jordan: We've done escrow for a couple enterprise accounts, it's an extra legal and ops lift but feasible. We'll add that to the doc.
[02:04] Aisha: Pricing note — procurement will need a clear path to pricing approval, we need an example chargeback model including egress. The RFP team flagged egress fees as a blocker.
[02:12] Evan: On egress we can provide a line item; egress is billed separate based on region egress tiers. For Dedicated we can often bake in predictable egress allowances for a committed tier.
[02:21] Diego: Clarify 'egress' — external egress to other cloud regions or to customer S3? We need both numbers for cost forecasting.
[02:28] Sofia: Right so typical egress buckets: intra-region traffic (negligible), cross-region egress (charged), and object storage egress to customer's bucket — depends on cloud provider rates. We'll provide a sample table.
[02:39] Jordan: Let's talk SLA. Our standard Hosted SLA is 99.5 for API availability with credits, Dedicated can be 99.9 with a shorter RTO and jitter SLO. But customers often want token-level latency SLOs too.
[02:51] Priya: We care about latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for our synchronous user flows. Can we put p95 < 300ms for typical prompt lengths?
[02:59] Sofia: For Dedicated we can get p95 around 120–220ms depending on model size and batching. For Hosted that's more variable. Note that token length and batching policies change numbers.
[03:12] Priya: Is that the benchmark you used in the pilot? The spike events we saw — were those KV cache misses or queueing on the shared tier?
[03:18] Sofia: The initial transcripts show spikes during burst windows; those look like capacity contention and some cold KV cache behavior. We saw some runs with higher tail latencies when sequences hit >1k tokens. Diego, any thoughts on your expected distribution?
[03:31] Diego: We're heavy on short queries, median ~60 tokens but we do have embedding jobs that are longer. Peak bursts at end of day. We can provide a sample day-of-week heatmap.
[03:40] Jordan: Good. On security we touched KMS and SSO. Any other compliance requirements — PCI, HIPAA, FedRAMP?
[03:48] Luca: Not PCI but we're evaluating FedRAMP for certain contracts; for now ISO and SOC2 are must-haves. Also DPA specifics: deletion timelines, subprocessors list, data flow diagrams.
[04:00] Jordan: We'll send DPA variant with subprocessor list and a proposed 30-day deletion window, can adjust if you need shorter.
[04:07] Aisha: For procurement we need billing terms — net45 or net30? Also if we commit to Dedicated reserved capacity we need a monthly invoice with usage reconciliation.
[04:16] Evan: We typically do net30, can do net45 for enterprise deals with procurement approval. For Dedicated we provide monthly invoices and a reconciliation process for overages.
[04:24] Aisha: Great. Also a question about termination for convenience and data return/escrow — what's standard?
[04:30] Jordan: Standard is 30-90 day notice for convenience. Data return can be in customer-owned S3 with encryption; escrow for source is separate and charged. We'll flag all these in the MSA.
[04:40] Luca: Two specific redlines: 1) limitation of liability carve-outs for confidentiality breach and data protection (we want higher cap), 2) mandatory notification window for breaches 48 hours rather than 72.
[04:52] Jordan: We'll push on breach notification to 48 where feasible; liability caps are negotiable but tied to commercial terms. For higher caps we usually require additional procurement approvals.
[05:02] Priya: On the pilot acceptance criteria — we need a clear definition of 'successful pilot' to move to production. What metrics do you propose?
[05:10] Sofia: Proposal: Availability >99.5 during pilot, p95 latency below agreed number (say 300ms), accuracy/evaluations not degraded compared to baseline prompts (we can codify with evaluation prompt set), and throughput — sustained X RPS for Y minutes. Also no P1 sev incidents tied to model drift during pilot window.
[05:30] Priya: Sounds reasonable. We'll provide the prompt set and expected thresholds.
[05:35] Diego: We'll also require a runbook for incident escalation and an on-call contact during the pilot.
[05:40] Evan: We'll provide a runbook template and add a dedicated on-call during acceptance.
[05:43] Aisha: Procurement will also ask for invoicing contact and PO process.
[05:47] Jordan: noted.
[05:48] Luca: One more thing: subcontractor subprocessors — can Redwood commit to 30 days notice for new subprocessor additions?
[05:55] Jordan: We do 30 days notice in many DPAs, yes.
[05:59] Priya: On dedicated capacity pricing — can you sketch the delta vs hosted? We're trying to model cost/TPS for committed 3-month and 12-month terms.
[06:08] Sofia: Quick back-of-envelope: for your workload (based on pilot 300k monthly inference calls, average tokens small), Hosted baseline would be pay-as-you-go; Dedicated reserved can lower per-request cost by ~25–40% depending on commitment and batching. There's also a fixed monthly fee for reserved GPU pools. We'll follow up with a custom cost sheet.
[06:25] Priya: Do you support quantized models on Dedicated? That impacts both cost and latency.
[06:29] Sofia: Yes, Dedicated supports quantization profiles and kernel-level optimizations; we'll include recommended quant configs for your model family.
[06:36] Diego: Network isolation — can we route through our VPC peering? We need to avoid public internet egress.
[06:42] Jordan: For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and private endpoints; for Hosted you can use private peering with a partner interconnect. We'll capture the architecture diagrams.
[06:52] Aisha: From procurement perspective, two blockers: a definitive egress pricing table and confirmation of KMS/CMK support in-region. Without those procurement can't approve.
[07:02] Jordan: Understood. Action: Sofia to share egress table + Dedicated costed example; Jordan to send MSA redline and DPA variant with 30/48 hr notification options.
[07:12] Luca: Also please include an explicit clause for data return format and timeline on termination — that's often requested by our privacy team.
[07:19] Jordan: We'll add a data disposition section with export to customer S3 encrypted and a 30-day retention prior to deletion unless otherwise requested.
[07:27] Priya: On the acceptance benchmark, can Redwood run 3rd party synthetic tests or do we run locally? We prefer Redwood to run the baseline to ensure reproducibility.
[07:35] Sofia: We can run a joint benchmark — we'll run a server-side run and provide logs and traces, and you can re-run locally if desired. We'll agree on seed prompts and traffic shape.
[07:45] Diego: Make sure traces include KV cache hit rates, batching window stats, and GPU utilization. Those were missing from initial pilot.
[07:52] Sofia: noted, we'll include KV cache metrics and tail-latency breakdown by token length.
[07:58] Aisha: Procurement will need a revised commercial summary that shows committed discounts and any termination liabilities — please include early termination fees if there's a reserved capacity commitment.
[08:09] Evan: We'll outline termination / refunding of prepayments in the pricing summary.
[08:14] Jordan: Any competitors you're evaluating?
[08:16] Priya: We looked at ModelCorp for hosted simplicity and CloudInferenceX for an on-prem option, mostly to benchmark pricing and security posture.
[08:24] Jordan: helpful to know.
[08:26] Luca: timeline — procurement wants to get this signed by end of December to hit Q1 rollout. Is that feasible?
[08:34] Jordan: Yes with a focused redline cycle and one legal touchpoint per side we can aim for signature by late December. We'll need procurement approvals and PO commit from Hypernova by mid-December to schedule Dedicated capacity for January.
[08:46] Aisha: That sounds ok. We'll try to lock internal approvals by Dec 10.
[08:51] Jordan: Great. Quick recap and next steps?
[08:54] Sofia: I'll send the Dedicated cost sheet, egress pricing table, and latency/throughput examples by Nov 22.
[08:59] Jordan: I'll share MSA redlines and DPA variant by Nov 20, plus a one-page commercial summary.
[09:05] Luca: I'll circulate our mandatory DPA clauses and confirmation on escrow requirements by Nov 23.
[09:10] Priya: We'll send the pilot prompt set, sample traffic patterns, and peak TPS numbers by Nov 24.
[09:16] Aisha: Procurement will confirm net terms and PO process by Nov 23.
[09:20] Evan: I'll coordinate the onboarding runbook and set up a 30-minute ramp call next week; propose Nov 24 or 25.
[09:27] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else?
[09:29] Diego: no, just ensure runbook has SLO contacts.
[09:31] Jordan: Okay thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and drop the redlines in the shared drive.
[09:36] Aisha: Thanks.
[09:37] Luca: Thanks all.
[09:38] Priya: Bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap, some acronyms transcribed oddly (KV cache -> K V cash), product names sometimes lowercased. There were several short dead-air pauses captured.

References mentioned: shared drive link to MSA draft (link: https://redwood-hosted.example/msa/hypernova-draft), DPA template (link: https://redwood-hosted.example/dpa/variant), Dedicated cost template (internal doc).

End of transcript.
